Let \(P=\sum_{i<j} v_i\cdot v_j\). Then
\[
\|S\|^2=7+2P.
\]
If a vector \(w=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\) with \(0<\theta<\pi/2\) is not on an axis, let the sum of the other six vectors be \(T=(A,B)\), where \(A,B\ge 0\). If \(A\le B\), replace \(w\) by \((1,0)\). Its contribution to \(P\) becomes \(A\), while originally it was
\[
w\cdot T=A\cos\theta+B\sin\theta\ge A(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)\ge A.
\]
Similarly, if \(B\le A\), replace \(w\) by \((0,1)\). Thus moving interior vectors to an axis cannot increase \(\|S\|\).

So the minimum occurs when all vectors lie on the coordinate axes. If \(a\) vectors lie on the \(x\)-axis and \(7-a\) on the \(y\)-axis, then
\[
S=(a,7-a),\qquad \|S\|=\sqrt{a^2+(7-a)^2}.
\]
This is minimized for \(a=3\) or \(a=4\), giving
\[
\|S\|=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5.
\]

\[
\boxed{5}
\]
